newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB says under upgrade review by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: AIB says under upgrade review by Moody's.

text.p: Allied Irish Bank Plc said on Thursday that it has been placed under review for a possible upgrade of its long-term ratings by Moody's Investors Service.
AIB said in a statement that the ratings of First Maryland Bancorp and the long and short-term ratings of Dauphin Deposit Corporation, both AIB subsidiaries, were also under review.
"AIB's fundamental performance has improved consistently over recent years, enhanced by the strong franchise value of its domestic Irish banking activities," AIB quoted Moody's as saying.

AIB announced on January 21 that its U.S. unit First Maryland Bancorp had agreed to buy Pennsylvania bank holding company Dauphin for $1.36 billion, the biggest acquisition ever made by an Irish company.
The statement said the following ratings are under review for possible upgrade:
AIB Plc-senior long-term debt and bank deposits, at A1; subordinated debt, at A2; junior subordinated debt, at A3; preferred stock at "a2".
First Maryland Bancorporation-subordinated and junior subordinated debt, at Baa1; preferred stock, at "baa1"; commercial paper rating, at Prime -2.
First National Bank of Maryland-long-term bank deposits and other senior and counterparty obligations, at A2;
First Omni Bank, NA-long-term bank deposits and other senior obligations, at A3; short-term bank deposits and other senior obligations, at Prime-2.
York Bank and Trust Company-long-term bank deposits and other senior and counterparty obligations, at A3;the ratings for short-term bank deposits and other senior obligations, at Prime-2.
Dauphin Deposit Bank & Trust Company-long-term bank deposits and other senior and counterparty obligations, at A2; the rating for short-term bank deposits and other senior obligations, at Prime 2.
